question: Which sensory area is tested to specifically confirm radial nerve function in a patient with a humeral shaft fracture?

answers.text: Palmar surface of the index finger (median nerve territory)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The palmar aspect of the index finger is median nerve territory. Radial nerve sensation is tested on the dorsum of the hand.

answers.text: First dorsal web space (dorsum of the hand between thumb and index finger)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The first dorsal web space is the autonomous territory of the superficial branch of the radial nerve — the most reliable area to detect radial nerve sensory loss after humeral shaft fracture.
The hypothenar eminence is supplied by the ulnar nerve (C8, T1). Ulnar nerve injury is more common around the elbow, not the humeral shaft.
The regimental badge area over the lateral deltoid is the key sensory test for the axillary nerve — relevant for proximal humerus fractures and shoulder dislocations.

overallFeedback.feedback: The radial nerve's autonomous sensory zone is the first dorsal web space on the dorsum of the hand. Always test and document this before and after any intervention for a humeral shaft fracture.
Correct. The first dorsal web space is the autonomous cutaneous zone of the radial nerve and the go-to test in humeral shaft fracture assessment.
